sources.entry: Gerbera - UPnP Media Server, which allows you to stream your digital media throughout your home network and listen to/watch it on a variety of UPnP compatible devices. (Source Code) GPL-2.0 Docker/deb/C++

summary.one_liner: Gerbera is a GPL-2.0 UPnP media server that streams a home media library to UPnP-compatible renderers and devices on the local network.
summary.what_it_does: It scans directories and extracts metadata from audio, image and video files (the README names MP3, OGG, AAC, M4A, FLAC, WavPack and JPG among others) and serves them over UPnP. A web UI shows a tree view of both the database and the filesystem for adding, removing, editing and browsing media. Transcoding is handled through plugins or scripts, and the server layout can be defined from extracted metadata. Directories are rescanned on a timer or via inotify, and it can serve external URLs, generate video thumbnails on the fly, and scrobble to last.fm. The README lists a long set of optional libraries that enable extra features such as MKV, EXIF, and alternate MySQL/MariaDB or PostgreSQL databases.
use_cases: stream home video and music to a smart TV
serve a media library to UPnP renderers on the home network
transcode media for playback on devices that lack codec support
organize a media server by file metadata
serve internet links to a UPnP renderer
how_to_run: git clone <repository URL (not given in the README text)>
notable: Web UI with a tree view for managing the database and filesystem
Automatic rescans by timer or inotify
User-defined server layout based on extracted metadata
Optional alternate UPnP stack (libnpupnp) and database backends (MySQL/MariaDB, PostgreSQL)
caveats: Many features depend on optional libraries that are disabled by default, such as ffmpeg, libexiv2, wavpack and lastfmlib
libupnp and libnpupnp are alternatives; one of the two is required to build
Full installation and build instructions live in external online docs, not in the README
